state.identity_rule: The platform permits an identity to authenticate only if its issuer and subject are attached to the same user and the identity is not revoked at admission T. A signed and unexpired token does not override a revoked identity.
state.revoked: Identity I is revoked before T. Its JWT remains signed and unexpired. An operator grant exists for the associated user.
state.twopass: Identity source I and operator source O provide linearizable reads and unique non-resetting increasing positions. All identity and operator first-pass reads complete before T. All identity and operator second-pass reads begin after T. Each second pass returns the same exact position as its own first pass. Every change to either relevant state advances that source position.
state.identity_change: A first fresh identity read at time 1 returns position 4 and attached. A revocation commits at time 2 and advances position to 5. A fresh second read at time 4 returns position 5 and revoked. Admission time T is time 3.
state.disjoint: Identity I is attached from time 1 through time 2 and revoked at time 3. Operator O is revoked through time 3 and only granted at time 4. An identity read at time 2 says attached and a separate operator read at time 5 says granted. No repeated reads are performed.
state.auth_and_revoke: At T an identity is attached, an operator grant is active, and the credential is unexpired. At time T+1 the identity is revoked. The policy allows an exact operation authorized at T to complete even after later revocation but refuses new admissions.
state.unknown_old: A source does not return a freshness or current position guarantee; two successive cached reads return matching values. Revocation may have committed before both reads.

revoked_rule.instructions: Under identity_rule, does the revoked identity in revoked qualify to authenticate at T?

unchanged_identity.instructions: In twopass, could I have changed and returned to its old state between its first and second reads without advancing its position?

common_point.instructions: Given all the stated conditions in twopass, did I and O both have their observed source states at T?

changed_revoked.instructions: In identity_change, is the identity revoked at T?

changed_accept.instructions: In identity_change, can a rule requiring equal first and second positions accept this proof?

disjoint_both.instructions: In disjoint, was there any time when identity I was attached and operator O was granted simultaneously?

already_admitted.instructions: In auth_and_revoke, may the exact operation already authorized at T finish after identity revocation?

cached_proof.instructions: In unknown_old, do equal cached values prove that no revocation committed before the reads?

infra_established.instructions: Does the hypothetical twopass establish that a particular deployed source actually implements linearizable reads?
